question: Why was the Cyrene-based separation of cathode scraps run at room temperature?
rendered: The excerpts do not mention running the Cyrene-based separation of cathode scraps at room temperature. They mention that the separation process should be kept above 90 °C, and that the PVDF binder dissolved in Cyrene at ~90 °C, and that phase separation occurred when the PVDF/Cyrene solution was cooled down to room temperature.
